description: Hi! We’re Team GeoNova, four students from Islamabad: Ali Hassan, Laiba Rafi, Arsal and Abdul Rauf. With Python, ML, GIS and remote sensing skills, we’re building a tool to select NASA Earth science variables, visualize how they change over time, and test whether those trends are statistically significant. Passionate about space tech for climate solutions. 🚀🌍
summary: Team GeoNova developed Himalaya Trend Lab, an interactive FastAPI and 3D/2D scrollytelling web platform that transforms 45 years (1981–2026) of NASA satellite observations and Meteomatics high-mountain weather data into a rigorous cryosphere detective workbench across Pakistan’s 9 glacier basins, 15 hotspots, and 10 Earth science variables. To address the challenge, it separates true long-term climate signals from mountain-weather noise by removing 12-month seasonal cycles, computing outlier-resistant Theil–Sen slopes with 95% confidence intervals, correcting autocorrelation with Hamed–Rao Modified Mann–Kendall tests, and applying Benjamini–Hochberg FDR spatial masking alongside 4 Machine Learning models (GPR changepoints, Random Forest drivers, 36-month forecasting, and K-Means/Isolation Forest hazard detection) and plain-language verdicts. This is vital because Pakistan’s 7,253 glaciers sustain 240 million people and 15,827 MW of hydropower via the Indus River while threatening communities with deadly Glacial Lake Outburst Floods—requiring trustworthy trend analysis and 7-day GLOF early warning.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Himalaya Trend Lab (Team GeoNova) is a FastAPI + interactive 3D/2D web platform analyzing 45 years (1981–2026) of NASA satellite and Meteomatics weather data across Pakistan’s 9 glacier basins, 15 hotspots, and 10 variables. Users pick a region, variable, significance threshold (α), and RGI v6.0 glacier mask to remove 12-month seasonal cycles and compute Theil–Sen slopes (95% CI), Hamed–Rao Mann–Kendall tests (autocorrelation-adjusted), Benjamini–Hochberg FDR spatial maps, and 0°C isotherm/dark-ice physics. It also integrates 4 Scikit-Learn ML models (GPR changepoints, Random Forest drivers, 36-month forecasting, K-Means/Isolation Forest), HimalayaShield 7-day GLOF radar, Indus Peak Water simulations (2020–2080), Detective Missions, and CSV/1-page PDF exports.

Benefits & Impact:

Separates true climate trends from mountain-weather noise across Pakistan’s 7,253 glaciers—supporting GLOF early warning (e.g., Shisper/Karakoram Highway), water and hydropower planning for 240M people (Tarbela Dam), climate research, and STEM education.

Tools & Stack:

Python 3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, joblib, ReportLab, pytest, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, SVG, GitHub, and Vercel; powered by NASA (MODIS, MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, GLDAS, AIRS, OMI, SRTM), RGI v6.0, NOAA indices, and Meteomatics APIs.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Turns rigorous climatology into an interactive "Trend Detective" experience with a 3D orbital terrain canvas, side-by-side basin comparisons, and honest statistical caveats. Built for autocorrelation safety (Hamed–Rao VIF), FDR spatial control, elevation-band physics (6.5°C/km lapse rate), and offline-resilient MD5 caching.
